name: Lemmy
description: Federated link aggregator and discussion platform over ActivityPub — Reddit-alternative on the fediverse. Posts, comments, communities, votes; remote Lemmy/Mastodon/Kbin users can follow your communities and comment cross-server.
author: Crow

install_consent_messages.en: Lemmy joins the public fediverse over ActivityPub — your instance becomes publicly addressable at the domain you configure, any community you host or post you publish can be replicated to federated servers (other Lemmy instances, Kbin, Mastodon, Friendica) and cannot be fully recalled. Lemmy's pict-rs image cache grows with federated content: 5-20 GB within weeks is typical on an active instance. Lemmy is hardware-gated to refuse install on hosts with <1 GB effective RAM after committed bundles; warns below 4 GB total. Because Lemmy's federation is community-scoped rather than user-scoped, a single large community can pull heavy content from many remote instances — monitor disk. Hosting illegal content (CSAM, credible threats) is your legal responsibility — major hubs (lemmy.world, lemmy.ml) may defederate your instance if reports go unaddressed.
install_consent_messages.es: Lemmy se une al fediverso público vía ActivityPub — tu instancia será direccionable en el dominio que configures, cualquier comunidad que hospedes o publicación que hagas puede replicarse a servidores federados (otras instancias de Lemmy, Kbin, Mastodon, Friendica) y no puede recuperarse completamente. El caché de imágenes pict-rs de Lemmy crece con el contenido federado: 5-20 GB en semanas es típico en una instancia activa. Lemmy está limitado por hardware: rechazado en hosts con <1 GB de RAM efectiva tras paquetes comprometidos; advierte bajo 4 GB totales. Como la federación de Lemmy es por comunidad (no por usuario), una sola comunidad grande puede traer contenido pesado de muchas instancias remotas — monitoriza el disco. Hospedar contenido ilegal (CSAM, amenazas creíbles) es tu responsabilidad legal — los hubs principales (lemmy.world, lemmy.ml) pueden dejar de federarse con tu instancia si los reportes no son atendidos.

env_vars.name: LEMMY_HOSTNAME
env_vars.description: Public hostname, bare (no https://, no path), e.g. lemmy.example.com. Lemmy stores it in every federated identity at its first start, so choose it before installing.

env_vars.name: LEMMY_DB_PASSWORD
env_vars.description: Password for the bundled Postgres role. Generated by Crow at install; never shown.

env_vars.name: LEMMY_PICTRS_API_KEY
env_vars.description: Shared secret Lemmy uses to talk to pict-rs. Generated by Crow at install; never shown.

env_vars.name: LEMMY_ADMIN_PASSWORD
env_vars.description: Password of the first Lemmy admin (username admin_pending). Crow generates it at install and saves it in Settings → Passwords (this machine only); Lemmy creates the admin with it on its first start against an empty database; change it after your first login.

env_vars.name: LEMMY_JWT
env_vars.description: Admin login JWT: POST /api/v3/user/login with username admin_pending and the admin password from Settings → Passwords, then paste the returned jwt here.

env_vars.name: LEMMY_URL
env_vars.description: Internal URL the MCP server uses to reach Lemmy's API (default http://lemmy:8536 over crow-federation).

notes: Four containers (lemmy + lemmy-ui + postgres + pict-rs); data lives in two Docker volumes (database, images), removed by uninstall with delete data. On its first start Lemmy creates the admin admin_pending with the generated password saved in Settings → Passwords; log in with it, then change the password and rename the account or add your own admin. lemmy-ui does not proxy the API: the public site must send /api, /pictrs, /feeds, /nodeinfo, /.well-known and ActivityPub requests (Accept: application/activity+json) to lemmy:8536 and the rest to lemmy-ui:1234. caddy_add_federation_site takes one upstream, so that split is a hand-written Caddy site for now. Federation, registration and captcha are site settings in Lemmy's Admin → Settings (Lemmy 0.19 does not read them from its config file). Licensing: Lemmy and lemmy-ui are AGPL-3.0 (image labels: AGPL-3.0-or-later), pict-rs is AGPL-3.0-only, Postgres uses the PostgreSQL License. Crow pulls the unmodified upstream images and runs them as separate containers, so Crow's own code stays MIT; a hosted Crow offering that runs Lemmy for other people must offer them the source of the Lemmy version it runs, including any changes (AGPL section 13).
